steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A database is an organised, structured collection of data that can be easily accessed, managed, and updated. A relational database stores data in multiple linked tables that relate to each other.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A table is a structured set of data organised in rows and columns. Each table stores data about one type of entity (e.g. a table for Students, a table for Courses).

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A field is a single category of data within a table. Each field has a name and a data type (e.g. text, integer, date). A field stores one piece of information for each record.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A record is a single, complete set of data in a table. Each row represents one item or entity, containing values for every field.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the definitions: table, field, record, primary key, foreign key Primary key = unique identifier; Foreign key = link to another table Always explain WHY primary keys must be unique (to identify each record) For redundancy questions, give a concrete example of duplicated data Remember: M:N relationships need a linking table to resolve Be able to draw simple E-R diagrams showing 1:1, 1:M, and M:N relationships
